senses.gloss: (cmp. b. h. עָשַׂק) (with ב) to work at, be engaged in. Sifra K’dosh., ch. VIII, Par. 4 ועוֹסֵק בו; Yalk. Lev. 619 ועוֹסְקֵנִי בו and busy myself with him (to punish him), v. עֵסֶק II.
units: <cite ref="Berakhot 11a:4">Ber. 11ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 6:7">Deut. VI, 7</cite>, ‘when thou sittest in thy house’) <he>פרט לעוסק במצוה</he> this exempts (from reading the Sh’ma) him who is engaged in a religious work; <cite ref="Sukkah 25a:6">Succ. 25ᵃ</cite>.

<cite ref="Sukkah 25a:11">Ib.</cite> <he>והעוסק במצוה פטור מן המצוה מהכא נפקא וכ׳</he> is it from here (Deut. l. c.) that we derive the rule, that he who is engaged in a religious act is exempt from other religious duties? Ib. 26ᵃ.

<cite ref="Pesachim 50b:5">Pes. 50ᵇ</cite> <he>לעולם יַעֲסוֹק אדם בתורה וכ׳</he> let man by all means be engaged in the study of the Law and the pursuit of religious work, even if not for their own sake &c., v. <cite ref="U01408"><he>שֵׁם</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Pesachim 50b:10">Ib.</cite> <he>וכל העוֹסְקִין במלאכת שמים</he> and all those who make a living of religious work (deal in objects used for religious ceremonies &c.); <cite ref="Pesachim 50b:10">ib.</cite> <he>ואם עוסקין לשמה וכ׳</he> but if they do so from a religious motive &c.; a. fr.—Part. pass. <cite ref="P01037"><he>עָסוּק</he></cite>; pl. <he>עֲסוּקִין</he>.
<cite ref="Ketubot 103b:17">Keth. 103ᵇ</cite> <he>ר׳ חייא ע׳ במצות הוה</he> R. Ḥ. was always engaged in some good work (charity).
<cite ref="Tosefta Bikkurim 2:15">Tosef. Bicc. II, 15</cite> <he>וכל העסוקין לגבוה</he> all whose business is connected with religion, v. supra.
<cite ref="Tosefta Bikkurim 2:15">Ib.</cite> <he>אם היו ע׳ לשום שמים</he>, v. supra.

<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 20:5">Ex. R. s. 20</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Exodus 13:19">Ex. XIII, 19</cite>) <he>כל ישראל היו ע׳ בכסף וכ׳</he> while all Israel were busy taking along silver and gold, Moses was busy getting the bones of Joseph; a. fr.

<cite ref="Mishnah Yoma 1:7">Yoma I, 7</cite> <he>ומַעֲסִיקִין אותו</he> and they entertain him (to keep him awake); <cite ref="Yoma 19b:14">ib. 19ᵇ</cite> <he>לא היו מעסיקין אותו וכ׳</he> they did not entertain him with music, but with their mouth (speech); <cite ref="Tosefta Yoma 1:9">Tosef. ib. I, 9</cite>.
Ib. לעַסְּקוֹ בהברה (not בהברא, Pi.) to keep him awake with noise (recitations).
<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 7:16">Midr. Till. to Ps. VII</cite> <he>היו מַעֲסִיקוֹת אותו עד שיבוא שמואל</he> they kept him engaged (in talk) until Samuel came; a. e.

<cite ref="Mishnah Sotah 1:9">Sot. I, 9</cite> <he>מי לנו גדול מיוסף שלא נ׳ בו אלא משה</he> who is greater than Joseph, to whose body none attended but Moses himself? (v. supra); <he>מי גדול ממשה שלא ני בו וכ׳</he> who is greater than Moses in whose burial none but the Lord himself was engaged? <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 25">Lev. R. s. 25</cite> <he>מתחלת ברייתו … לא נ׳ וכ׳</he> soon after the creation the Lord was first of all engaged in planting (<cite ref="Genesis 2:8">Gen. II, 8</cite>), <he>אף אתם לא תִתְעַסְּקוּ וכ׳</he> even so, when you enter the land, you shall apply yourselves first of all to planting (<cite ref="Leviticus 19:23">Lev. XIX, 23</cite>). Y. Ḥag. II, 77ᵇ <he>וישבו ונִתְעַסְּקוּ</he>, v. <cite ref="P01053">next w.</cite> Tanḥ. Vaëra 5 (play on <he>הָעשֶׁק</he>, <cite ref="Ecclesiastes 7:7">Koh. VII, 7</cite>) <he>עסק שנ׳ שלמה … הטעהו</he> (not <he>הטעוהו</he>) the occupation with vain things in which Solomon engaged, led him astray; <cite ref="Ecclesiastes 7:7">ib.</cite> <he>כשהחכם מִתְעַסֵּק בדברים הרבה מערבבין וכ׳</he> when a scholar engages in too many affairs, they confound him so that he loses his wisdom; <cite ref="Ecclesiastes 7:7">ib.</cite> <he>חכם המתעסק בצרכי צבור משכחין וכ׳</he> if a scholar busies himself with public affairs, they cause him to forget his learning; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Tosefta Arakhin 4:27">Tosef. Arakh. IV, 27</cite> <he>מִתְעַסֵּק בירק בקדרה בכל יום</he> may arrange to have vegetables in the pot every day; <he>מתעסק ירק בקדרה ואלפס וכ׳</he> (read: <he>בירק</he>) may have vegetables in the pot and stew &c.

senses.gloss: to do a thing without a direct practical purpose; to practice, experiment.
units: <cite ref="Shabbat 157b:2">Sabb. 157ᵇ</cite> <he>מתעסק בעלמא אנא</he> I was merely playing (without the intention of measuring).

<cite ref="Mishnah Rosh Hashanah 4:8">R. Hash. IV, 8</cite> (<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 32b:24">32ᵇ</cite>) <he>אבל מִתְעַסְּקִין בהם כדי שילמדו</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>מתע׳ עמהם עד</he>) but you may practice with them that they may learn (to blow the Shofar); <he>והמתעסק לא יצא</he> and he who merely blows for practice, has not done his duty. Ib. 33ᵃ <he>מתע׳ בהן עד שילמדו וכ׳</he> (Tosef. ib. IV (II), 10 <he>מתלמדין לתקוע</he>) you may practice with them …, even on the Sabbath; a. e.

senses.gloss: to do one thing while intending to do another thing; to miss one’s purpose, choose the wrong thing.
units: <cite ref="Sanhedrin 62b:13">Snh. 62ᵇ</cite> <he>המתעסק בחלבים וכ׳</he> he that misses his purpose in selecting forbidden fat to eat (intending to reach out for a permitted piece), or in consanguineous connection (by mistaking the person) is bound to bring a sin offering; <he>המתע׳ בשבת</he> who does a forbidden act by mistake on the Sabbath (meaning to do a different though forbidden act); <cite ref="Keritot 19b">Kerith. 19ᵇ</cite>.

<cite ref="Mishnah Keritot 4:3">Ib. IV, 3</cite> (<cite ref="Keritot 19a:58">19ᵃ</cite>) (ref. to <he>אשר חטא בה</he>, <cite ref="Leviticus 4:23">Lev. IV, 23</cite>) <he>פרט למתעסק</he> this is to exempt him who sinned by doing the thing which he had not intended to do. Ib. 19ᵇ <he>מתעסק דמאי</he> to what kind of a mistaken act does this refer? Ib. <he>מתע׳ בדבר דלאו מצוה</he> if by mistake he did an act which was not commanded (for that day). Ib. <he>מתע׳ בחבורה</he> making a wound (on the Sabbath) by mistake (circumcising the wrong child), opp. <he>מקלקל בחבורה</he> doing harm by making a wound; a. fr.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 8:2">Gen. R. s. 8</cite> <he>עד שמלאכי השרת מדיינין … ומתעסקין אלו עם אלו וכ׳</he> while the ministering angels were arguing with one another, disputing with one another, God created him (Adam); a. e.
